summary.headline: H.G. Infra Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue INR974 crore with 25.6% EBITDA margin, but PAT fell to INR80 crore from H1 PAT of INR35 crore after weak H1 execution.
summary.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue was INR883 crore with EBITDA margin of 11.9% and PAT of INR32 crore (3.6% margin), versus INR67 crore in Q2 FY26. Management guides to roughly INR4,200 crore of revenue in H2 FY27 and INR6,000 crore-plus by year-end, with EBITDA margins recovering to 13-14% from Q3, though it did not expect margins to return to 15%+ in the next one to two years. Order book stood at INR13,685 crore as of 26 September 2026, and FY27 order inflow target is INR10,000-11,000 crore against about INR5,500 crore secured to date. Working capital remained elevated, with contract assets at INR2,100-2,165 crore, and management expects a significant reduction by year-end.

segments.name: Roads and highways (incl. HAM and EPC)
segments.commentary: Order book INR8,792 crore, about 64% of total. Pune-Shirur (awarded via Welspun, INR3,931 crore) is in mobilisation with appointed date expected by mid-December; management targets about INR600 crore from Pune in H2 and about INR700 crore for FY27.

segments.name: Rail and metro
segments.commentary: Order book INR2,883 crore, about 21% of total. Management expects about INR1,400 crore of rail and metro revenue in H2 FY27; Kanpur, Gaya-Son Nagar, Karanjgaon and Dhule-Nardana have time-extension requests pending due to land and work-front constraints.

segments.name: Renewables and BESS
segments.commentary: Renewables order book INR610 crore including BESS. Solar projects about 96% complete; Banaskantha and Dholera BESS civil works about 80% and 60%; three BESS projects (about 1,470 MWh with GUVNL and NVVN) expected to generate about INR225 crore annual revenue on commissioning, with H2 BESS revenue assumed at about INR350 crore.

segments.name: Transmission and distribution
segments.commentary: T&D order book INR1,400 crore across Angul (Odisha), Jamshedpur (Jharkhand) and Mirzapur (UP); Angul has financial closure and TSA signed. Management assumes about INR300 crore of transmission revenue in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue expected at about INR4,200 crore, with Q3 near INR800-900 crore and Q4 about INR3,000-3,500 crore; management cited roughly INR6,000 crore run-rate by year-end.
EBITDA margin expected to recover to 13-14% in Q3 and Q4 FY27 and to remain in that range in FY28.
FY28 revenue target of about INR7,000 crore, described as 'quite possible' by management.
FY27 order inflow target of INR10,000-11,000 crore against about INR5,500 crore secured to date; about INR7,000 crore of bids pending results and INR5,000-6,000 crore expected in H2.
Standalone gross debt target of INR900 crore by end FY27; finance cost of about INR80 crore in H2 and INR110-120 crore in FY28; capex of about INR50 crore in H2 and INR100-120 crore in FY28.

Remaining HAM monetisation holdback of about INR550 crore expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27; standalone gain on these deals estimated at about INR70 crore; Karnal Ring Road monetisation cash receipt expected around Q2 FY28.
capex_capacity: Pune-Shirur project appointed date expected by late November or early December 2026; Capital Region Ring Road Package III also expected around the same time.

Solar projects (Anuppur, Mirzapur) at about 96% completion as of 30 September 2026, with delays from monsoon, transmission line and land issues; revised completion expected in the next few months. Project debt 89% sanctioned, with INR215 crore+ to be released in Q3 and Q4 FY27 after commissioning.
BESS: long-lead items including BESS and PCS delivery expected by January 2027; Banaskantha and Dholera expected to commission by March 2027, Choraniya around June 2027.
Equity requirement across HAM, transmission, BESS and solar is about INR3,050 crore, of which INR1,846 crore infused as of September 2026.
demand_pricing: Management said commodity price increases hit rail (OHE and S&T work), BESS and transmission; highway work is protected by real-time bitumen and crude POL escalation, while steel, cement and aggregates impact is limited.
BESS margin was earlier expected above 20% but is now about 12% after accounting for currency and battery price moves.
Transmission bids reportedly include price escalation for aluminium and copper, which management says are up 30-40%+ against bid levels.

Management sees pipeline opportunities in MSRDC expressways (re-tendered after cancellations), RSRDC Rajasthan expressways, Ahmedabad Metro (about INR7,000 crore of projects), and Jaipur and Delhi metro bids (about INR1,300 crore).

qa_highlights.question: What is the gain and tax impact from the four monetised HAM assets, and when will it hit the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no equity gain given net worth; about INR550 crore of collections is pending from the four assets plus AP-1, and standalone gain is about INR70 crore, expected in Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin outlook, and what does H2 require?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about INR6,000 crore of revenue by year-end, with H2 about INR4,200 crore and margins of 13-14% from Q3, after mobilisation in several large projects.

qa_highlights.question: Is unbilled revenue included in the INR13,685 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book excludes executed contract assets; it is the balance yet to be executed, so it converts to revenue as work proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: Why is contract asset rising, and when will it fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed INR580+ crore to rail (10% retention payable on commissioning) and the rest to HAM variation items and monetised projects; contract assets are expected to fall by INR700-800 crore by year-end to INR1,200-1,500 crore by March.

qa_highlights.question: What drove other income and the Maharashtra interest item?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR18 crore of interest income on Maharashtra projects was booked in other income, not revenue; further reconciliation claims may bring in smaller amounts.

qa_highlights.question: When will margins recover to 15%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was not confident margins return to 15%+ in the next one to two years, citing geopolitical commodity prices and competition.

risks_watch: Execution depends on appointed dates for Pune-Shirur, Capital Region Ring Road Package III and Odisha Gobindpur-Tangi, expected in late November to mid-December; further delays would push H2 revenue below the INR4,200 crore target.
Rail projects face land and work-front constraints, with extension requests pending for Kanpur, Dhule-Nardana, Gaya-Son Nagar, Karanjgaon and Thane Metro land and social issues.
Standalone margin of 11.9% in Q2 and consolidated PAT of INR35 crore in H1 point to weak bottom line; management does not expect a return to 15%+ margins soon.

Working capital and contract asset build-up (INR2,165 crore) and trade payables down to INR1,188 crore from INR1,633 crore; cash conversion depends on INR550 crore holdback and Karnal monetisation timing.
Commodity exposure in BESS and transmission, with BESS margin reset to about 12%; cancellations and disqualifications in UPEIDA and UP tenders affect inflow visibility.
key_quotes: So we are expecting to be roughly around INR6,000 -odd crores by end of this year, if you see.
Probably at the current scenario, it does not look like because of the geopolitical commodity prices as well as the competition all across entire infrastructure.
We are not very much confident that the coming one to two years is going to be better.
The plateau has been reached in last quarter only. Now significant drop is likely to be there, be it, say, if you see the debt part, if you see the contract asset part
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth, H2 ramp-up and order inflow, with mobilisation and appointed dates cited as the basis. Cautious and non-committal on margins, saying it is not confident of a return to 15%+ within one to two years, and vague on several gain, tax and timing questions (for example the tax impact on monetisation, which was referred to the finance team).

adds.what: BESS projects about 1,470 MWh (GUVNL and NVVN), expected to generate about INR225 crore annual revenue on commissioning
Solar projects at Anuppur and Mirzapur about 96% complete

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 revenue of about INR4,200 crore and roughly INR6,000 crore run-rate by year-end, plus FY28 INR7,000 crore, backed by a INR13,685 crore order book and INR5,500 crore of FY27 inflow secured against a INR10,000-11,000 crore target, though the H2 ramp needs heavy execution from a weak H1 and pending appointed dates and time-extension requests.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides standalone EBITDA margin recovering to 13-14% in Q3 and Q4 from 11.9% in Q2, but does not expect 15%+ in the next one to two years given commodity and competition pressure.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Solar at Anuppur and Mirzapur about 96% complete, BESS about 1,470 MWh (Banaskantha and Dholera by March 2027, Choraniya around June 2027), with BESS revenue about INR225 crore annually on commissioning; delays from monsoon and transmission issues mean timing could slip.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Revenue guided to about INR4,200 crore in H2 FY27 (H1 was INR2,074 crore consolidated) and INR7,000 crore in FY28, backed by INR13,685 crore order book, though H2 depends on appointed dates for Pune-Shirur and Ring Road Package III in late Nov to mid-Dec.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management frames FY28 capex at only INR100-120 crore and H2 FY27 at about INR50 crore, with major Pune spend being light on equipment, so no large new capacity capex is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 consolidated PAT fell to INR35 crore from INR151 crore and management relies on a sharp H2 ramp that still depends on pending appointed dates, so an upgrade is not supported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Appointed dates for Pune-Shirur, CRRR Package III and Odisha are due late Nov to mid-Dec, rail time-extensions are pending for five projects, and H2 needs INR4,200 crore versus INR2,074 crore in H1, so slippage risk is high.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed; BESS and solar are existing project pipelines.

rows.label: Contract asset reduction of INR700-800 crore by year-end
rows.why: Contract assets at INR2,165 crore expected to fall to INR1,200-1,500 crore, helped by INR550 crore HAM holdback in Q3-Q4 and rail retention payable on commissioning, but trade payables already fell to INR1,188 crore from INR1,633 crore.

rows.label: Standalone gross debt to INR900 crore
rows.why: Gross debt is INR1,595 crore today and the target is INR900 crore, which depends on the INR550 crore monetisation collections and about INR215 crore+ solar project debt release after commissioning.

rows.label: FY27 order inflow INR10,000-11,000 crore
rows.why: About INR5,500 crore secured to date against the target, with about INR7,000 crore of bids pending and INR5,000-6,000 crore expected in H2, but cancellations in UP tenders weigh on visibility.

tone.note: Management was confident on the H2 ramp, FY28 INR7,000 crore revenue and order inflow, but cautious on margins (no return to 15%+ in one to two years) and vague on monetisation gains and tax; analysts pushed on the H2 revenue ramp and contract asset build.
